# XHelpers Pro 1.0.5
> Candidate notes for 1.0.5 (13). This version has not completed signed, > Apple-account, accessibility/localization-presentation, performance, or > owner-only release approval and has not been published. 1.0.4 (12) was > never published, so its changes are listed here.
## What's New
- Adds an optional Xin account. Sign in with an email address and password, an emailed sign-in code, Google, or Sign in with Apple, then enroll the account in XHelpers, link your local Pro license to it, and manage the linked sign-in methods from the Account window. Every local tool and local Pro activation keeps working signed out and offline; the account is never required. The Account window can delete XHelpers data, the whole Xin account, or just the sign-in identity, each with a fresh sign-in and each resumable if interrupted. Session and recovery state stay in this Mac's Keychain, and XHelpers Pro never stores a Google or Apple password. The privacy policy and license agreement describe exactly what the account service keeps. - Live Subtitles can now show captions in the spoken language without translating. Switch between Translate and Captions only at the top of the Configure window's Languages section, or flip the Captions Only row in the status menu, which restarts a listening session in the new mode. The status-menu row, shortcut, and Configure window are now titled Live Subtitles. - Adds Quick Audio, a fast local player for user-supplied MP3, M4A (AAC or ALAC), AAC/ADTS, WAVE/BWF, AIFF, AIFF-C, FLAC, and CAF files, with an ephemeral queue that is discarded when the player closes. - Makes the supported formats available in Open With without taking over defaults; Audio Player Settings provides a separate opt-in action and can restore the previous default handlers while XHelpers Pro still owns them. - Adds Music & Playlists for browsing and playing songs made available through Apple Music and for creating private playlists owned by XHelpers Pro. Apple Music access is requested only after you choose Connect, never at launch, and the feature does not create or change playlists in Music.app. Provider-safe live queues can be extended, replaced, or explicitly saved as a new XHelpers Pro playlist. - Adds Local Audio playlists and a private on-Mac index for only the files and folders you select, with source reauthorization, missing-file repair, and separate delete/reset controls that never change the original audio files. - Adds Local Video to Music & Playlists: a private on-Mac index of only the video files and folders you select, with its own sources, missing-video repair, source reauthorization, and a separate delete control. It obeys the same source-authorization and deletion rules as Local Audio and never changes the original video files. Choosing a video plays it in Quick Video, and a Quick Video queue can be saved as a Local Video playlist. - Stores Music & Playlists data in XHelpers Pro's private, size-bounded local SQLite database with up to three daily recovery snapshots. Successful provider-data deletion or full reset clears all Music & Playlists recovery snapshots and database recovery/journal files. The app declares file-timestamp access for user-selected files and directories under Apple's required privacy-manifest reason 3B52.1. - Adds Extract Audio for pulling the soundtrack out of videos into new M4A (AAC or Apple Lossless), MP3, or WAV files, or copying AAC, Apple Lossless, and PCM tracks without re-encoding. Videos are never modified and outputs never overwrite existing files. MP3 output uses the bundled LAME encoder library, disclosed in the third-party notices. - Adds Quick Video, a small floating player for the formats QuickTime plays (MP4, MOV, M4V, 3GP), with speed, loop, always-on-top, frame stepping, and Picture in Picture. Any frame can be opened in Image Tools, added to the Screen Shelf, or copied, and the file can be sent straight to Extract Audio. Live Subtitles can run on the video being played, taken from the player's own audio and pinned to the player window. Video types are offered in Open With without taking over defaults; unsupported files are handed to your default video app. - Gives Quick Video a playback queue in the same list Quick Audio uses. Dropping files, Open Video…, and Open With add to the queue of the player you are already using instead of opening one window per file; rows can be reordered, played next, or removed, loop is now off, one, or all, and New Player Window starts a second, independent queue. The queue exists only while that window is open and is never saved. - Gives Quick Video the Audio Player's audio effects. Audio Effects… in the player's options menu opens the same panel, over the same settings kept per output device, so adjusting the chain in either place applies to both. A video's audio is processed as it plays, and Live Subtitles hear what you hear. - Gives both players the same queue controls: Shuffle, Repeat off, one, or all, and Play Next, which moves the rows you picked directly behind the one that is playing. Shuffle deals a fresh order each time you turn it on and skips a row it cannot play, exactly as the queue does. - Brings the Audio Player's features out of the ⋯ menu. Shuffle, Repeat, Audio Effects, Live Subtitles, and Add to Queue are now buttons under the transport, each showing its own state: shuffle and repeat light up while they are on, repeat says whether it is the whole queue or one song, Audio Effects lights up while the output you are listening on has effects applied, and Live Subtitles lights up while it is running for the player. The row stays in place with an empty queue, so adding files, shuffle, repeat, and the effects chain are still one click away, and the window is no taller than before. The ⋯ menu keeps the rarer things: Play Audio…, Audio Player Settings…, Reveal Current File in Finder, and Clear Queue. - Lets a live queue hold local audio and local video together. Songs play in Quick Audio and videos in Quick Video, so a mixed list keeps the music where it belongs and opens the picture where you can see it. Apple Music and YouTube still keep a queue of their own, and Music & Playlists now says so on Add to Queue before you press it rather than in a sheet afterwards. Saved playlists still hold one kind of item. - Offers the same media actions wherever an item appears. Extract Audio, Open Frame in Image Tools, Add Frame to Screen Shelf, Copy Frame, and Live Subtitles are decided in one place and shown by both player toolbars, the queue rows, and the Music & Playlists rows, each offering only what that item can really do: no Extract Audio for a song, no frame actions for a row that is not on screen, and Live Subtitles only for what is playing. - Runs Live Subtitles for a video on the player's own audio inside XHelpers Pro instead of tapping this app's audio process, so a video from your own library can be subtitled with nothing else listened to. Browser audio still uses the process capture it always did, and the subtitles overlay is still pinned to the player window. Subtitle text, captured frames, and queues are still never saved. - Adds Image Tools for straightforward resize, crop, rotate, flip, markup, redaction, format conversion, metadata choices, and bounded batch output. - Adds Capture to Clipboard and Capture & Mark Up to the existing Screen Tools selector, keeping captures in memory until an explicit destination is chosen. - Expands local health guidance into Why Is My Mac Slow?, combining plain- language CPU, memory, startup-volume, and thermal evidence with safe actions. - Adds PDF Quick Actions for combining PDFs, organizing pages, extracting or splitting pages, and creating PDFs from images, with a PDF-only Finder action. - Adds Startup & Background Inspector for reviewing login items and background agents with direct System Settings guidance. - Retains the existing opt-in memory monitoring engine as part of Mac Health's broader local slowdown evidence. - Adds Text Tools and a first-class Text Editor for plain text and Markdown, including split/preview layouts, syntax highlighting, and text-size controls. - Adds private, on-device Live Translated Subtitles for selected browser audio, with speaker-aware cues and fullscreen tracking on macOS 26.4 or later. - Expands file and Markdown viewing with multiple windows, large-text, binary, hexadecimal, and persistent text-size support. - Reorganizes the menu bar into a compact two-column layout with keyboard access to its submenus and clearer utility and screen-tool groups. - Improves Window Recall activation/focus verification and keeps Snap & Arrange state current, keyboard-accessible, and stable after submenu refreshes. - Improves subtitle placement across fullscreen Spaces and stabilizes speaker colors, source lines, and translated cues.
## Initial 1.0.0 Highlights
- Introduces XHelpers Pro as the direct-download flagship Mac utility app. - Includes display tools for mirrored MacBook display blackout, brightness, contrast, dim-until-key-press, and keyboard backlight control. - Adds optional Auto Wi-Fi Switch for saved Wi-Fi networks, with signal threshold controls and local-only Wi-Fi scanning. - Adds Finder context menu actions for creating files and folders, pasting copied items, copying paths, and opening Finder selections in configured apps such as TextEdit, Terminal, Codex, Claude, or VSCode. - Adds local Safe archive actions for encrypting selected files or folders into a `.safe` file, adding items to an existing Safe, and decrypting Safes back to local folders. - Lets users configure the default terminal, default editor, enabled Finder menu items, saved folder grants, Full Disk Access guidance, and copy-path escaping. - Ships with a new XHelpers Pro icon and Sparkle update support.
## Install
1. Open the DMG. 2. Drag `XHelpers Pro.app` onto `Applications`. 3. Open XHelpers Pro from Applications.
The app appears in the macOS menu bar.
## Compatibility
Compatibility note: this direct-download app uses macOS capabilities that may not be suitable for a Mac App Store build and may change in future macOS updates.
Requires macOS 14.0 or later.
